extra.message: SQL injection via id parameter — Full read access to users table including password hashes/plaintext and session tokens; potential DB manipulation [verified: id param string-concatenated into SQL query, no parameterization (attacks.py:39).]

Command injection via domain parameter — Remote code execution as the server process user [verified: domain param concatenated into shell command string with shell=True, no sanitization (attacks.py:165-170).]

Insecure pickle deserialization of client-supplied object — Remote code execution as the server process user [verified: pickle.loads on client-supplied base64 object with no allow-list/integrity check (attacks.py:199).]

SQL injection / auth bypass via password parameter — Authentication bypass and arbitrary SQL execution against the users table [verified: password param concatenated raw into SQL string despite username filtering (attacks.py:289).]

Backdoor route executes URL path as shell command — Full remote code execution as the server process user [verified: do_BDR passes self.path[1:] directly to subprocess.check_output with shell=True and no sanitization, gated only by a risk-level check with no auth control.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file read via path parameter — Disclosure of arbitrary files readable by the server process (secrets, config, credentials) [verified: path opened via os.path.abspath(path) with no base-dir restriction (attacks.py:211).]

Session fixation via session parameter — Attacker can hijack the victim's authenticated session using a session ID they chose in advance [verified: session param written directly into cookie with no regeneration, and AuthBypass writes session into users table on login (attacks.py:229-231, 297).]

Path traversal in static file handler — Disclosure of arbitrary files on the filesystem readable by the server process, including source code and secrets outside the web root [verified: StaticHandler.find opens './{}'.format(path) with no normalization or containment against a root directory, allowing '../' traversal to read arbitrary files.]

Reflected XSS via msg parameter — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in victim's browser session, enabling session/cookie theft [verified: msg param returned unescaped as content, rendered via template substitution (attacks.py:71-77).]

Stored XSS via guestbook comment — Persistent JavaScript execution against every visitor viewing the guestbook, enabling mass session hijacking [verified: comment param stored unescaped and rendered back in table with no HTML-encoding (attacks.py:86-98).]

Open redirect via path parameter — Phishing via trusted-domain redirect to attacker site; combined with quote-breakout, also enables XSS [verified: path param inserted unvalidated into window.location.replace string (attacks.py:118-125).]

CSRF on account settings and account deletion endpoints — Attacker can change a victim's email or delete their account by luring them to a crafted link/page while authenticated [verified: email update and account delete are GET requests gated only on SESSIONID cookie, no CSRF token (attacks.py:322-324, 366-368).]

Stored XSS via unescaped email in settings form — Attacker-controlled markup persists in the email field and executes in the victim's browser session on /settings, enabling session/token theft or further account takeover. [verified: email settable via unescaped update (line 324) and rendered unescaped into value="{}" attribute (line 341), enabling stored XSS via attribute breakout.]

Session ID generated with insecure PRNG (Mersenne Twister) — An attacker able to observe/collect a few generated session tokens (or otherwise infer PRNG state) can predict future SESSIONID values and hijack other users' sessions without needing credentials. [verified: SESSIONID token is generated via random.sample (Mersenne Twister, non-cryptographic) and used as the sole session credential, with no secrets/os.urandom usage anywhere in the file.]

Session cookie missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags — Increases impact of XSS (cookie theft via document.cookie) and CSRF (cookie sent cross-site) and allows interception over unencrypted connections [verified: Only morsel['path']='/' is set in do_GET; no Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes are ever configured on the cookie.]
